concepts.name: Effect Events for non-reactive effect logic

questions.prompt: A React form rendered on the server needs stable IDs linking each field to its help text during hydration. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Generate a new random UUID on every independent server and client render
Use the array index as every help element's document ID
Use useId within each field for the accessibility relationship
Use useId as the form's database record primary key

questions.explanation: useId is intended for accessibility relationships and supports server hydration with matching component trees. Random per-render IDs can mismatch; it is not a persistent database identity or list-key generator.

sources.title: useId
sources.claim: useId supports accessibility attribute IDs and server hydration but should not generate list keys; matching server/client component trees are required.

questions.prompt: A React external store has not changed, but `getSnapshot` returns a fresh object on every call. Why can useSyncExternalStore repeatedly re-render?

choices.text: React treats each fresh snapshot as a changed value
React compares snapshot fields deeply and discovers hidden mutations
Returning an object silently removes the subscription callback
The hook polls until the snapshot object becomes mutable

questions.explanation: React requires the snapshot result to be cached when nothing changed. Fresh object identity looks like a new snapshot and can trigger repeated updates; this is not deep structural comparison.

sources.title: useSyncExternalStore
sources.claim: getSnapshot must return a cached immutable snapshot when the store is unchanged; subscribe returns an unsubscribe function.

questions.prompt: In React 19.2+, an effect should reconnect only when roomId changes but log the latest theme when a connection event fires. Which useEffectEvent statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: roomId remains a dependency when it controls reconnection
Effect Events are called from effects, not arbitrary click handlers
An Effect Event freezes theme at the component's initial render
An Effect Event can read the latest committed theme
An Effect Event should replace every dependency in the effect

questions.explanation: An Effect Event separates non-reactive logic that reads current values. The room still determines the reactive connection lifecycle. It is not a dependency escape hatch or a normal event-handler callback, and it does not freeze initial state.

sources.title: useEffectEvent
sources.claim: Effect Events read latest committed props and state without making that logic reactive; they are not a shortcut for omitting true dependencies and are called from effects.

sources.title: React 19.2
sources.claim: React 19.2 introduced useEffectEvent to separate effect-fired event logic from reactive synchronization dependencies.

questions.prompt: A React list already has stable database IDs for its items. Should a component call useId to generate their list keys?

choices.text: Yes, because useId sorts keys into server rendering order
No, list keys should come from the item data
Yes, because generated IDs persist when an item leaves the list
No, because list keys must always equal an array index

questions.explanation: useId is for generated accessibility IDs. List identity belongs to the data, so use the stable item IDs rather than generated IDs or array positions.

sources.title: useId
sources.claim: useId supports accessibility attribute IDs and server hydration but should not generate list keys; matching server/client component trees are required.

questions.prompt: An external store internally mutates an array. What should its useSyncExternalStore getSnapshot function return while that array has not changed?

choices.text: A new copied array on every call, even without a store update
The mutable array, changed in place without a new snapshot identity
A promise that resolves after the next store mutation arrives
The same cached immutable snapshot until the data changes

questions.explanation: Mutable stores need immutable snapshots, cached until the underlying data changes. Both unnecessary new objects and changing one mutable object in place break the snapshot contract.

sources.title: useSyncExternalStore
sources.claim: getSnapshot must return a cached immutable snapshot when the store is unchanged; subscribe returns an unsubscribe function.

questions.prompt: A developer uses useEffectEvent to hide a value that should trigger an effect to resynchronize. Which review conclusions fit its contract? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Effect Events intentionally always read only the first render's state
True reactive dependencies should remain in the effect
The hook is a universal replacement for useCallback in UI handlers
Non-reactive effect logic may read the latest committed values
Using it to conceal reactive dependencies is the recommended pattern

questions.explanation: Effect Events provide current values to non-reactive effect logic. They are not a universal callback utility or a way to conceal values that truly require resynchronization, and they do not read only initial state.

sources.title: useEffectEvent
sources.claim: Effect Events read latest committed props and state without making that logic reactive; they are not a shortcut for omitting true dependencies and are called from effects.

sources.title: React 19.2
sources.claim: React 19.2 introduced useEffectEvent to separate effect-fired event logic from reactive synchronization dependencies.
